items.text: Finite = integral + finite type; finite $\Rightarrow$ proper (affine hence separated, finite type, and integral $\Rightarrow$ universally closed).
Stable under base change, so it suffices that $f$ is closed. A closed immersion is finite ($A/J$ is finite over $A$).
Reduce to $f(X)$ closed: replace $X'$ by the induced reduced structure, $Y$ by the closure of the image; then $X,Y$ reduced, $f$ dominating, and one must show $f$ surjective.
Y=\operatorname{Spec}A,\ X=\operatorname{Spec}B,\ B\ \text{integral over }A,\ A\subset B:\qquad \forall\,\mathfrak p\subset A\ \exists\,\mathfrak P\subset B,\ \ \mathfrak P\cap A=\mathfrak p
